title: Credential-leak guard: scanners for logs, frames, telemetry, backups and CI
goal: A shared secret scanner built from the contract's `secret-patterns.json` and wired into logging, REST and WebSocket frames, telemetry ingest, CI and backup/restore, so a provider credential that reaches the backend by mistake is rejected or redacted and never stored, logged or echoed.
scope_in: Package `packages/core/src/secret-guard/`: `loadPatterns()` reads `contracts/fixtures/providers/secret-patterns.json` at build time (generated module `patterns.generated.ts`, checked against the file by a test) and compiles the 7 regexes once; `scanText(text, o?)`, `scanJson(value, o?)` (walks keys and string values, depth cap 32, node cap 100 000), `redactText(text)` -> replaces each match with `[redacted:<pattern id>]`.

Speed design: a trigger prefilter (`indexOf` for `sk-`, `eyJ`, `access_token`, `refresh_token`, `id_token`, `uthorization`, `AKIA`, `AIza`) so clean text never runs a regex; large inputs scanned in 64 KiB windows with a 512-byte overlap (a match needs at most its 4-20 character prefix to be detected, so the overlap is enough to detect a match split across windows). Budget: under 50 microseconds per KiB for typical log lines and JSON bodies (no match present).

Surface 1, logger: `createGuardedLogger(base: Logger): Logger` that runs message and context through `redactText`/`redactJson` before they reach the B005 logger, increments `centcom_secret_guard_hits_total{surface="log",pattern=<id>}` (labels are ids only) and logs one `secret_guard_hit` warning with the pattern id and surface, never the text.

Surface 2, request and frame scanning: `guardRestBody(body, headers)` returned as a Fastify `preValidation` hook factory `secretGuardHook()` (`fastify.ts`) rejecting with `400 invalid_request` (CT-ERR, generic detail `request rejected`) when a body, query or header value except the `Authorization` header of the service's own auth scheme matches; `guardFrame(frame): { ok: true } | { ok: false; code: 'invalid_frame' }` (`frame.ts`) scanning only the **clear** parts of a WebSocket envelope (`t`, `k`, ids and the clear payload `p`), answered with `sys.error` `invalid_frame` by the relay lane that mounts it. Neither ever logs the matching text; they log `{surface, pattern id, frame kind or route, size}` only.

Surface 3, telemetry ingest: `guardTelemetryBatch(events): { clean: TelemetryEvent[]; rejected: number }` rejects any event whose JSON contains a match (counted under drop reason `pii_pattern` by the ingest lane), responding `204` as the contract requires.

Surface 4, CI: `tools/ci/secret-guard-scan.mjs` and `.github/workflows/secret-guard.yml` scanning the repo tree (excluding `contracts/fixtures/providers/secret-patterns.json` and the lane's own `must_match` test constants, via the allow-list by id and path), all fixtures, a directory of log files, and a database dump file given as an argument; exit 1 with `file:line:pattern-id` (never the text) on a hit.

Surface 5, backup/restore hook: `scanBackupStream(readable, o): Promise<{ scannedBytes: number; hits: { pattern: string; offset: number }[] }>` streaming with the same windows, and `backupScanHook` that the backup/restore lane (B099) calls before an upload completes and after a restore finishes; a hit marks the artefact `quarantined` in the returned report and fails the drill step.

Allow-list for false positives: `secret-guard.allow.json` entries `{ pattern_id, scope: 'path'|'route'|'log_component', value, reason, expires }` matched by pattern id plus location, **never by matching content**; an entry without `reason` or past `expires` is a config error; at most 20 entries, loaded through B004 config.

Ciphertext rule: frames are scanned only in their clear fields; the `ct` field (and any base64url blob) is never decrypted, decoded or scanned, and the scanner is given no key material. A helper `stripCiphertext(frame)` is the only way frames reach `scanJson`.
scope_out: The logger itself, redaction of generic PII and request-context handling (B005); relay privacy canaries (B050); telemetry schema validation and retention (B085); this lane provides the scanner and adapters, and the owning lanes mount them.
Backup mechanics, DR drills and restore tooling (B099); this lane supplies the scan hook only.
Scanning or decrypting encrypted frame payloads; the relay has no keys by design (CT-CRYPTO).
Detecting non-provider secrets beyond the contract's patterns (generic entropy scanners) and any client-side redaction (the client has its own).
Adding or changing patterns (a contract change).
build_against: Pure functions tested with the contract fixture `contracts/fixtures/providers/secret-patterns.json` (`must_match` and `must_not_match`), in-memory Fastify instances and frame objects from `contracts/fixtures/events/`, a fake logger sink, and a generated 50 MiB dump stream; no real client, relay or database is needed (the B011-style simulator can be used for end-to-end checks in the mounting lanes).
interfaces: `createGuardedLogger(base: Logger, o?: { metrics: Metrics }): Logger`; `secretGuardHook(o?: { allow?: AllowList; metrics?: Metrics }): preValidationHookHandler`; `guardFrame(frame: unknown): { ok: true } | { ok: false; code: 'invalid_frame'; pattern: string }`; `guardTelemetryBatch(events: unknown[]): { clean: unknown[]; rejected: number }`; `backupScanHook(stream, ctx: { artefact: string }): Promise<{ quarantined: boolean; hits: number }>`.

REST rejection body (CT-ERR problem+json): `{"type":".../invalid_request","title":"request rejected","status":400,"code":"invalid_request","request_id":"req_..."}`, same text for every pattern (no pattern id echoed to the caller).

Metrics: `centcom_secret_guard_hits_total{surface=log|rest|frame|telemetry|backup|ci, pattern=<id>}` (counter), `centcom_secret_guard_scan_seconds{surface}` (histogram). Alert rule documented in the README: any hit on `rest|frame|telemetry|backup` pages the on-call (a client bug or an attack), `log` hits open a ticket.
CLI: `node tools/ci/secret-guard-scan.mjs [--root .] [--dump <file>] [--logs <dir>] [--json]` -> exit 0 clean, 1 hits (listing `path:line pattern-id`), 2 usage error.

Config via B004: `SECRET_GUARD_ENABLED` (default `true`; setting false is allowed only when `NODE_ENV=test`), `SECRET_GUARD_MAX_BODY_BYTES` (default 1 048 576 for scanned REST bodies; larger bodies are already rejected by the size limit).
acceptance: All 4 `must_match` strings of the contract fixture produce exactly one `Hit` each with the expected `pattern` id, and all 4 `must_not_match` strings produce 0 hits, in `scanText`, in a JSON value at depth 5 (key and value positions), and inside a 300 KiB text window boundary at offsets 65 535 and 65 536.

Performance: scanning 1 MiB of typical JSON log lines (no secrets) takes under 51 ms on the CI runner (< 50 microseconds per KiB), and a worst-case 1 MiB of `sk-` repeated tokens completes in under 2 s with no catastrophic backtracking (ReDoS test with a 10 s timeout).

`createGuardedLogger(base).info('x', { token: 'sk-ant-api03-AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAA' })` writes a line to the sink that contains `[redacted:anthropic_api_key]` and not the token, increments the hit counter once, and logs a `secret_guard_hit` warning without the text.

A `POST` through `secretGuardHook()` with a body containing `Authorization: Bearer abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789` returns 400 `invalid_request` with the generic body above, the request handler is not called, nothing in the captured logs or metrics labels contains the value, and an identical clean body returns 200.

`guardFrame` rejects a clear-part `p` containing `AKIAABCDEFGHIJKLMNOP` with `invalid_frame`, accepts every frame in `contracts/fixtures/events/` and accepts a frame whose `ct` is base64url text that happens to contain `sk-ant-` characters (ciphertext not scanned); a spy proves `ct` is never read by `scanJson` (stripCiphertext removes it first).
`guardTelemetryBatch` drops a batch event carrying a secret and keeps the other 99 events of a 100-event batch; the response status stays 204 in the mounting test.

`node tools/ci/secret-guard-scan.mjs` exits 1 on a fixture tree with a planted key, printing `path:line pattern-id` and no matched text, exits 0 on the real repo (the contract pattern file and test constants are covered by allow-list entries of scope `path`), and `--dump` scans a 50 MiB stream in under 5 s using under 64 MiB of memory.
`backupScanHook` on a stream with a key split across two 64 KiB windows reports 1 hit with the right offset and `quarantined:true`; on a clean stream `quarantined:false`.

Allow-list: an entry for pattern `openai_api_key` at path `docs/` suppresses a hit in `docs/x.md` but not in `src/x.ts`, and the same text in `docs/` that matches a different pattern id is still reported; an entry without `reason` makes config loading throw; there is no API that accepts a content string to allow.
tests: secret-guard/patterns.test.ts: contract must_match / must_not_match, generated module equals the contract file, pattern count.
secret-guard/scan.test.ts: windows and overlap, depth and node caps, unicode, property test that `redactText` output never matches any pattern and that scanning is idempotent.
secret-guard/perf.test.ts: 50 us/KiB budget with a generous CI margin factor of 2 reported as a warning and 5 as failure, ReDoS corpus.
secret-guard/logger.test.ts, fastify.test.ts, frame.test.ts, telemetry.test.ts: one file per surface, including 'no matched text in logs, metrics or responses'.
secret-guard/ciphertext.test.ts: `ct` never scanned or decoded, no key material in the module's imports (static check).
secret-guard/backup.test.ts and ci-cli.test.ts: split-window match, quarantine result, CLI exit codes and output.
secret-guard/allow.test.ts: by-id and by-location only, expiry, missing reason, cap of 20.
guardrails: MUST NOT log, return, store or put into a metric label the matched text, a prefix or suffix of it, or its hash; hits are reported as `{pattern id, surface, location, length}` only. A guard that echoes the secret defeats its purpose.
MUST NOT scan, decode or attempt to decrypt `ct` or any ciphertext/blob field; the relay and API never hold keys (CT-CRYPTO 3) and decrypting for scanning would break the trust model.

False positives are handled only by allow-list entries naming a pattern id and a location with a reason and an expiry; never by allowing a content string or by weakening a pattern here. Pattern changes are a contract PR.

Fail closed on rejection surfaces (REST, frames, telemetry): if the scanner throws, the request or frame is rejected with the generic error, not passed through; the logger surface fails open to a fixed `[unscannable]` placeholder instead of dropping the log line.
Rejection responses MUST be identical for every pattern and MUST NOT reveal which pattern or field matched (an oracle for probing).
The scanner runs in the request path: no synchronous scan of more than 1 MiB per request, windowed scanning yields to the event loop every 256 KiB, and a hard per-request budget of 20 ms.
failure_modes: Pattern file missing or invalid at build time -> build fails; at runtime the generated module is used, so the service still starts with the last good patterns.

A pattern produces a false positive in production (e.g. an identifier containing `sk-` followed by 20 URL-safe characters) -> add a scoped allow-list entry with an expiry through config, redeploy; rejected clients get the generic 400 until then; the alert runbook lists the check.
Scan exceeds the 20 ms per-request budget -> reject with 413 `payload_too_large` for REST or `frame_too_large` for frames rather than skipping the scan.
Backup stream read error mid-scan -> hook returns failure (`quarantined:true, reason:'scan_incomplete'`) and the drill step fails; a partial scan never counts as clean.
Metrics backend down -> counters buffer in memory up to 1 000 samples then drop with a debug log; scanning and rejection are unaffected.
notes: CONTRACT GAP (pattern quality): `openai_api_key` is `sk-(proj-)?[A-Za-z0-9_\-]{20,}` with no word boundary, so ordinary text such as `task-management-system-overview` (contains `sk-management-system-overview`) matches, and it also matches every `sk-ant-` key (two ids fire on one string). The fixture's `must_not_match` list does not include such cases. Suggested contract fix: add a leading `(?<![A-Za-z0-9_])` and test cases; until then the allow-list by location is the only remedy and the REST/frame surfaces may see false 400s for free text fields, which in practice are inside `ct` and not scanned. Also `eyJ...` three-part JWT-like strings legitimately appear in the project's own access tokens (CT-AUTH); `Authorization` headers of our own scheme are excluded from REST scanning for that reason, but JWTs in bodies are still rejected. The mounting lanes (api plugins, relay, telemetry ingest, backup) must add the one-line mount; this lane does not edit their files. The card is S-sized but the five surfaces plus CI is a full day; SPLIT? the CI scan and backup hook if it overruns.
